subject: Switching order of indicators in latent variable definition changes results

messages.author: d247a5c717b79a83
messages.subject: Switching order of indicators in latent variable definition changes results
parts:
I want to do a path analysis with lavaan but encounter a few problems and would appreciate any help.


The structural model looks like this:



The relation between one observed independent (s) and one observed dependent variable (v) is mediated through a latent variable (m) that is defined by two observed indicator variables (x1, x2). This corresponds in part to the SEM example in the tutorial on the lavaan project website.

When I enter the code (given in the attached text file, code.txt) into R, I encounter two problems:

(1) The results change when I change the order of the indicator variables.

This model:

    # measurement model
        m =~ x1 + x2

returns a different result than this model:

    # measurement model
        m =~ x2 + x1

How can that be? Isn't the order of the indicators arbitrary? And if not, how do I know which is the correct order, if my model does not presuppose a specific order?

(2) There are a few warnings that I don't understand but which seem to be related to the fact that my data contains missing observations (NA).

What do I have to do to obtain reliable estimates?

messages.subject: Re: Switching order of indicators in latent variable definition changes results
parts:
# measurement model
        m =~ x1 + x2

does not match your diagram.  The diagram has x1 and x2 predicting m, while the syntax has x1 and x2 dependent on m, along with v.  To conform to the diagram, specify x1 and x2 as predictors of m.
     Moreover, if m is meant to be a common factor, the statistical model will not be identified, unless you impose some constraints.
     If you want to capture the joint effects of x1 and x2 predicting s, I suggest Heise's (1972) "sheath coefficient" concept:
http://smr.sagepub.com/content/1/2/147.short
--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: Re: Switching order of indicators in latent variable definition changes results
parts:
Thank you, Ed.

I accidentally drew the arrows from x1 and x2 towards m. That is of course wrong, they should go from m to x1 and x2. That is, following the example in the SEM tutorial on the lavaan website, m is the latent variable behind x1 and x2.

What constraints do I need to impose to identify the model?

I'm not sure I understand the article you recommend. x1 and x2 are not nominal as ethnicity is in the article. "m" is a behavior, x1 is the average frequency of this behavior per hour, x2 is the average duration (in seconds) of this behavior per hour. Both are ratio scaled (I believe), having a definite zero (zero times, zero seconds). And both x1 and x2 are determined by the latent variable behavior (m). But my English may not be good enough to understand the difference between "determined by" and "determinant of".

Maybe, given these explanations, you could elaborate on your answer a bit?

Am Samstag, 26. September 2015 15:45:06 UTC+2 schrieb Edward Rigdon:
Manfred--
     Your syntax:
  # measurement model
        m =~ x1 + x2
does not match your diagram.  The diagram has x1 and x2 predicting m, while the syntax has x1 and x2 dependent on m, along with v.  To conform to the diagram, specify x1 and x2 as predictors of m.
     Moreover, if m is meant to be a common factor, the statistical model will not be identified, unless you impose some constraints.
     If you want to capture the joint effects of x1 and x2 predicting s, I suggest Heise's (1972) "sheath coefficient" concept:
http://smr.sagepub.com/content/1/2/147.short
--Ed Rigdon
